jurisdiction.name: Togo
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Togo has no AI-specific law or published AI strategy. AI is governed indirectly by the 2019 personal data protection law, which restricts decisions based solely on automated processing, and by a 2025 communiqué from the data protection authority (IPDCP) setting its expectations on platforms using published personal content to train AI systems. A national AI strategy and an AI governance framework within a planned Digital Code are in preparation.

Instance de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (IPDCP)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the Official Journal and the digital ministry's and data protection authority's websites. The cybersecurity agency's and the National Assembly's websites could not be accessed, and the cybersecurity laws are only available as scans that could not be searched. The national AI strategy, the Digital Code and the cybersecurity laws are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: Law No. 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on the protection of personal data
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly; promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Published in the Journal officiel de la République togolaise, 64th year, No. 26 ter (special issue) of 29 October 2019. Art. 97 provides that the law is executed as a law of the State; no separate entry-into-force date is stated, and Art. 95 gives existing processing a compliance period from entry into force. The supervisory authority it creates, the IPDCP, publishes the law on its own site and is operational. No AI-specific law exists in Togo as of 11 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Togo's general data protection law regulating the collection, processing, transmission, storage and use of personal data, with declaration and prior-authorisation regimes (e.g. for biometric, genetic and health data) and data-subject rights including access, opposition (Art. 45) and rectification. Art. 27 bars court decisions that assess a person's conduct, and any decision producing legal effects, from being based solely on automated processing intended to profile the person or evaluate aspects of their personality. It creates the Instance de protection des données à caractère personnel (IPDCP) as the independent supervisory authority with sanctioning powers.

instruments.summary: Public notice from Togo's data protection authority warning that some digital platforms plan to use users' published content (texts, images, comments, interactions) to train AI systems and that this raises privacy issues. Citing the right to object in Art. 45 of the 2019 data protection law, it tells users they may refuse such use, explains how to lodge an objection through platforms' privacy settings, and urges users not to publish sensitive data.
